hints: Look carefully at the structure and notice that not all -OH groups are the same type in malic acid.
Count how many carboxylic acid $-CO_2H$ groups and how many alcohol $-OH$ groups are present in one molecule.
Think about which reagent is specific for esterification of an alcohol, while bases and metals attack the acidic protons instead.
walkthrough:
**Identify the three -OH groups**

Malic acid has two different functional groups. It contains two carboxylic acid groups, $-CO_2H$, and one secondary alcohol group, $-CH(OH)-$.

So in total there are three $-OH$ groups, but of two different chemical types:
$$\text{malic acid} = 2 \times -CO_2H + 1 \times -CH(OH)-$$

**Recall what each reagent attacks**

Sodium, $Na$, reacts with all acidic H atoms, both alcohol and carboxylic acid, to give $H_2$. Bases like $NaOH$ and $NaHCO_3$ react with carboxylic acids to give salts, so they will react twice.

Only esterification with a carboxylic acid targets the alcohol $-OH$ selectively:
$$R-OH + CH_3CO_2H \rightleftharpoons CH_3CO_2R + H_2O$$

**Choose the selective reagent**

Ethanoic acid with concentrated $H_2SO_4$ catalyst esterifies the single alcohol group to form an ester, leaving the two $-CO_2H$ groups unchanged under these conditions.

That is the only reagent that reacts with just one $-OH$ group.

options.A: Correct. Ethanoic acid in acid conditions esterifies alcohols. Malic acid has only one alcohol -OH, so only that group forms $CH_3COO-CH$ ester. The two carboxylic acid groups do not esterify with ethanoic acid.
options.B: Sodium is not selective. It reacts with every labile H, giving $H_2$ gas. It will react with both $-CO_2H$ groups and the alcohol $-OH$, so three moles of H atoms per mole of malic acid.
options.C: Sodium hydrogen carbonate, $NaHCO_3$, reacts with carboxylic acids to give $CO_2$, but not with alcohols. Since malic acid is dibasic with two $-CO_2H$ groups, it reacts with two -OH groups, not one.
options.D: Sodium hydroxide, $NaOH$, neutralises carboxylic acids to give salts and water, but does not normally react with alcohols. Malic acid has two $-CO_2H$ groups, so two moles of $NaOH$ are needed, meaning two -OH groups react.
